meta.priceDisclaimer: All operator package ranges and DIY estimates are approximate, checked Nov 13, 2026. Confirm permit tariffs at district forest/tourism checkposts before departure.

treks.name: Kedarkantha Peak
treks.tagline: 360-degree snow ridge summit rising from oak meadows above Sankri
treks.statusNote: Open year-round except peak monsoon cloud cover; Sankri–Naitwar corridor gets busy Dec–Jan weekends.

permits.notes: Entry fee covers initial 3D/2N window (~INR 200 Indian / INR 600 Foreign + ~INR 50–250/extra day) plus refundable clean-trail security deposit.

treks.roadhead: Sankri (1,950 m) — 200 km / ~8–9 hr from Dehradun
highlights: Frozen pine-ringed Juda ka Talab basin at 2,780 m
Pre-dawn lantern ascent along an open 3,810 m ridgeline
Clear panoramas of Swargarohini, Bandarpoonch, and Black Peak (Kalanag)
Dense deodar, brown oak, and rhododendron belts below 3,100 m

elevationProfile.camp: Juda ka Talab to Base Camp

diyBudget.notes: Shared bus/Sumo Dehradun -> Purola -> Sankri (~INR 600–750 each way). Homestays/dhaba huts in Sankri are plentiful.

treks.summary: A classic winter and spring summit route in Uttarkashi where short daily trail distances still build significant elevation over four days. Ideal for prepared beginners seeking true snow-ridge walking.

treks.name: Hampta Pass & Chandratal
treks.tagline: Dramatic ecological divide linking lush Kullu meadows with barren Lahaul spires
treks.statusNote: Jul–Aug brings slippery scree & glacial river swells across Balu ka Ghera–Shea Ghoru; June & September offer clearest crossings.

permits.authority: HP Forest / Lahaul Checkpost (Chandratal vehicle permit if driving)
permits.notes: No paid trail entry fee for Indian foot trekkers; valid govt ID mandatory at Chatru/Jobra checkposts and green tax (~INR 100–200) if vehicles enter Spiti.

treks.roadhead: Jobra (2,980 m) via Manali hairpin road
highlights: Instant vegetation shift crossing the 4,270 m Pir Panjal saddle into arid Lahaul
Knee-deep cold stream wading near Shea Ghoru campsite
Glacial boulders and river plains at Chika & Balu ka Ghera
Optional crescent-lake excursion to Chandratal (4,250 m)

elevationProfile.camp: Balu ka Ghera to Shea Ghoru via Pass

diyBudget.notes: HRTC/shared cab Manali -> Prini -> Jobra and return Chatru -> Manali via Atal Tunnel.

treks.summary: Few trails pack such stark contrast into 26 km: green maple-walnut groves above Manali give way over a steep boulder pass into the stark desert valleys of Lahaul.

treks.name: Valley of Flowers & Hemkund
treks.tagline: UNESCO biosphere valley carpeting Pushpawati gorge in sub-alpine monsoon blooms
treks.statusNote: Open ~June 1 to Oct 4 annually; entry closed inside park after 2 PM and no overnight camping allowed inside the valley.

permits.authority: Nanda Devi National Park / Forest Checkpost, Ghangaria
permits.notes: Day entry permit capped (~300 visitors/day) issued at Ghangaria; Hemkund Sahib pilgrimage registration also mandatory via Uttarakhand govt portal.

treks.roadhead: Govindghat / Poolna (~1,850 m) from Rishikesh (270 km)
highlights: Hundreds of endemic orchid, blue poppy, and brahma kamal blooms mid-July to August
Strict day-use valley trail preserving fragile alpine meadows from Ghangaria base
Stone-paved Laxman Ganga gorge climb alongside cascading monsoon falls
Acclimatization hike option to Hemkund Sahib glacial tarn (~4,328 m)

diyBudget.notes: Easy DIY route: permanent dharamsalas/guesthouses in Ghangaria and clear cobblestone trail require no guide for standard day walks.

treks.summary: A heritage biodiversity sanctuary accessed from Ghangaria where trekkers stay in lodges rather than tents, exploring fresh alpine flora daily before returning below treeline.

treks.name: Triund Ridge
treks.tagline: Steep 22-switchback climb to a grassy crest beneath Dhauladhar granite spires
treks.statusNote: HP High Court & Forest Dept enforce a 400 trekkers/day & 20-tent limit at Gallu Devi checkpost; day hikers face ~11:30 AM entry cutoff.

permits.authority: HP Forest Department Checkpost (Gallu Devi / Indru Nag)
permits.notes: Day entry ~INR 100; legal overnight pitch fee ~INR 550 per 2-person tent (capped at 20 tents ridge-wide).

treks.roadhead: McLeod Ganj / Gallu Devi Temple (2,130 m)
highlights: Immediate dramatic wall view of Moon Peak and Dhauladhar ridge
Shade through oak and cedar slopes above Dharamkot
Short weekend format reachable overnight by Volvo from Delhi
Optional snow-line day walk toward Lahesh Cave (3,550 m)

diyBudget.notes: Self-guided route on marked trail; arrive at Gallu Devi checkpost before 8:30 AM to beat quota cutoff.

treks.summary: Northern India's classic first ridge walk above Dharamshala. Simple navigation and well-worn stone steps hide a steady 750 m climb in the final 22 switchbacks.

treks.name: Kheerganga Trail
treks.tagline: Forest riverside ascent through Barshaini waterfalls and geothermal Parvati springs
treks.statusNote: CRITICAL RULE (July 2024 – 2026): Overnight camping at Kheerganga meadow is banned by HP Forest Dept; stay in Kalga, Pulga, Nakthan, or Tosh homestays.

permits.authority: HP Forest Dept Barrier (Barshaini / Icy Point)
permits.notes: Barshaini checkpost logs photo ID (~INR 100) and enforces strict up-before-10 AM / descend-by-2 PM day-trek curfew.

treks.roadhead: Barshaini (2,200 m) — 16 km uphill from Kasol
highlights: Thundering Rudra Nag serpent cascade midway up the gorge
Sacred geothermal sulphur springs at 2,960 m overlooking snow ribs
Option to loop out via forested Pulga Fairy Forest & wooden bridges
Authentic wooden mountain homestays in Nakthan and Kalga

diyBudget.notes: Verify any operator NOT pitching tents illegally atop the meadow; stay legally in Kalga/Tosh guesthouses instead.

treks.summary: Following strict 2024 eco-protection orders banning meadow camps, Kheerganga has transformed into a rewarding early-start day hike out of Parvati valley wooden villages.

treks.name: Roopkund (Mystery Lake) Sector
treks.tagline: Sweeping emerald Ali & Bedni plateaus leading beneath Trishul's western icefall
treks.statusNote: Uttarakhand High Court orders ban overnight camping on alpine bugyals (Ali & Bedni meadows); check modified forest-line itineraries or alternative Ronti Saddle routes before booking.

permits.notes: Strict environmental limits restrict camping near high meadows above treeline; operators must obtain zone clearances.

treks.roadhead: Lohajung (2,350 m) — ~220 km from Kathgodam / Rishikesh
highlights: India's vastest high-altitude bugyal corridor across Ali & Bedni
Sheer towering proximity to Mt Trishul (7,120 m) & Nanda Ghunti
Steep glacial scree & snow chute ascent to 4,800 m glacial tarn
Stone temple ruins and historic Nanda Raj Jat pilgrimage trail

diyBudget.notes: Complex permit rules & rapid gain above 4,000 m strongly advise an experienced local Lohajung/Wan guide + porter team rather than going solo.

treks.summary: Famous for skeletal remains preserved around its high cirque tarn and iconic twin meadows, Roopkund requires careful acclimatization and adherence to strict meadow-preservation laws.

treks.name: Brahmatal Lake
treks.tagline: Quiet winter sanctuary looking eye-level across Trishul & Nanda Ghunti faces
treks.statusNote: Premier winter alternative when higher Chamoli passes close under deep drift.

permits.notes: Forest & eco-fee collected per entry + per-day tent charge at Lohajung forest beat office.

treks.roadhead: Lohajung (2,350 m) via Kathgodam or Rishikesh
highlights: Mirror-still Bekaltal oak forest pool before rising above treeline
Knife-edge Jhandi Top ridge run directly facing Trishul (7,120 m)
Frozen Brahmatal alpine amphitheater at 3,420 m
Oak and burans rhododendron canopies carpeted in powder snow

diyBudget.notes: Microspikes and warm gaiters essential Dec–Mar; rent cleanly at Lohajung/Kathgodam market.

treks.summary: Carved along a snow-draped horseshoe ridge opposite the Roopkund massif, Brahmatal pairs sheltered lake camps with exhilarating exposed crest panoramas.

treks.name: Har Ki Dun Valley
treks.tagline: Cradle of wooden Garhwali hamlets winding straight toward Swargarohini ice walls
treks.statusNote: Well-suited to endurance beginners willing to walk consecutive 10–12 km valley stages.

permits.notes: Park entry permit obtained at Sankri/Naitwar barrier; mandatory trekking guide/local check-in.

highlights: Century-old timber villages of Osla & Gangad with terraced millets
Parallel glacier-fed Supin and Ruinsara river valleys
Face-to-face silhouette of Swargarohini (I–IV) looming over the bowl
Rich alpine birds & occasional side-excursion to Marinda Tal

elevationProfile.camp: Kalkattiyadhaar to Har Ki Dun & back

diyBudget.notes: Village homestays at Gangad/Osla allow lighter packs than full self-supported tenting in spring/autumn.

treks.summary: Steeped in Garhwal legend along the ancient Tons valley, Har Ki Dun rewards steady endurance with dramatic cultural heritage and monumental valley glaciers.

treks.name: Dayara Bugyal
treks.tagline: Vast undulating Uttarkashi carpet rolling toward Bandarpoonch & Kala Nag
treks.statusNote: Open cleanly spring through deep winter; camping permitted at forest treeline camps (Gui/Chilapada), preserving meadows.

permits.notes: Forest checkpost entry near Raithal/Barsu; overnight pitch prohibited on active upper meadows — stay at forest-edge camps.

treks.roadhead: Raithal (2,200 m) or Barsu (2,250 m) — ~185 km from Dehradun
highlights: Kilometers-wide natural alpine downs rising to Bakaria Top (~3,654 m)
Historic wooden Panchpura bhawans in heritage village Raithal
Close sunrise sightline onto Srikanth, Jaonli, and Draupadi ka Danda
Gentle gradient ideal for families & first-time trekkers

elevationProfile.camp: Gui to Chilapada & Dayara Top loop

diyBudget.notes: GMVN guest houses & community homestays in Raithal keep base costs super affordable.

treks.summary: Arguably India's finest introductory meadow walk: emerald velvet in summer, rust-gold in autumn, and rolling white ski hills from December through February.

treks.name: Chopta–Tungnath–Chandrashila (+Deoria Tal)
treks.tagline: Forest tarn reflections rising to the world's highest Shiva shrine & a 360-degree summit
treks.statusNote: Chopta–Tungnath road can experience black ice / heavy snow closure mid-Jan–Feb; Deoria Tal trail stays crisp most of winter.

permits.notes: Deoria Tal entry & sanctuary trail fees collected at Sari village barrier; drone flights prohibited inside sanctuary.

treks.roadhead: Sari / Chopta (2,700 m) — ~205 km from Rishikesh
highlights: Dawn reflection of Chaukhamba I–IV across calm Deoria Tal
Blooming crimson rhododendron (Burans) tunnels each March–April
Historic stone temple complex at Tungnath (~3,490 m)
Wide Garhwal horizon from Chandrashila top (~3,680–4,000 m)

diyBudget.notes: Stone-laid path from Chopta -> Tungnath needs zero technical guide in clear weather; carry microspikes in Dec–Mar snow.

treks.summary: Compressed high-reward sanctuary circuit combining a forest mirror lake, ancient stone architecture, and big Kedar–Garhwal summits on a paved-then-alpine trail.

treks.name: Sandakphu & Phalut
treks.tagline: Binational tea-house ridge gazing directly at Everest, Lhotse, and Sleeping Buddha
treks.statusNote: Singalila National Park closes annually mid-June to mid-September for wildlife breeding & monsoon; **local guide mandatory for all trekkers**.

permits.notes: Mandatory local guide (~INR 1,200/day shared by group). Trail weaves along Indo-Nepal border ridge — foreign nationals must carry passports & Indian multi-entry visa precautions.

treks.roadhead: Manebhanjan (1,920 m) or Sepi — ~95 km from NJP / Siliguri
highlights: Sleeping Buddha skyline aligning Kanchenjunga, Pandim, and Kabru peaks
Rare sightline spanning both Kangchenjunga (East) and Everest–Makalu (West)
Cozy wooden trekkers' huts & tea houses across Tumling, Kalipokhri, Gurdum
Red panda & magnolia sanctuary forests

diyBudget.notes: Splitting the mandatory Singalila guide across 3–4 trekkers keeps tea-house DIY remarkably economical with hot food & beds every night.

treks.summary: India's premier tea-house ridge trail and only trek gazing effortlessly onto four of Earth's five highest peaks on clear autumn mornings.

treks.name: Goecha La (Kanchenjunga Viewpoint)
treks.tagline: Demanding Eastern Himalayan odyssey face-to-face with Kangchenjunga's southeast wall
treks.statusNote: Access restricted beyond Viewpoint 1 (~4,600–4,940 m) under conservation rules; foreign trekkers require Sikkim PAP (minimum 2 persons via registered operator/e-FRRO).

permits.notes: Indians: KNP park & camera/camp fee at Yuksom. Foreigners: Sikkim Restricted/Protected Area Permit (PAP) via indianfrro.gov.in + Sikkim Tourism — **solo foreign trekking banned (min 2 + agency guide)**.

treks.roadhead: Yuksom (1,780 m) — ~150 km / ~7–8 hr from NJP
highlights: UNESCO Khangchendzonga National Park cloud forest and suspension spans
Alpine dawn ridge panorama at Dzongri Top (4,150 m)
Mirror stillness at sacred emerald Samiti Lake (4,300 m)
Up-close vertical grandeur of Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) & Mt Pandim

elevationProfile.camp: Goecha La Viewpoint & back to Thansing

diyBudget.notes: Even budget independent teams must register via Yuksom certified local guide + yak/dzomo porter support due to Sikkim conservation law.

treks.summary: A monumental 10-day Eastern Himalayan expedition testing steep vertical endurance across monsoon-fed valleys to touch the footsteps of the world's third-highest peak.

treks.name: Markha Valley
treks.tagline: Rain-shadow Ladakhi barley oasis villages culminating atop 5,260 m Kongmaru La
treks.statusNote: Ladakh demands minimum 48-hour Leh acclimatization prior to trailhead departure; many trekkers now join at Chilling roadhead skipping Gandala.

permits.authority: Hemis National Park / Ladakh Environment & Wildlife Office
permits.notes: Indians require Ladakh Environment fee + Hemis NP daily wildlife ticket (ILP removed for most zones); foreigners need PAP in restricted sectors.

treks.roadhead: Chilling / Skiu (~3,200 m) — 65 km southwest of Leh
highlights: Teahouse/homestay sleeping warmth inside isolated Markha & Hankar farmhouses
Rain-shadow clarity during July–August when rest of Himalaya sees heavy rain
Elevated alpine plateau at Nimaling (4,800 m) beneath Kang Yatse II
Dizzying prayer-flag crossing over Kongmaru La (5,260 m)

diyBudget.notes: Village homestays along Chilling–Markha–Hankar charge ~INR 1,400–1,800/night inclusive of dinner, breakfast & packed lunch — eliminating heavy tents until Nimaling parachute camp.

treks.summary: Ladakh's iconic summer homestay trek blending Buddhist desert gorges, glacial braids, and a 5,260 m pass overlooking the towering north wall of Kang Yatse.

treks.name: Stok Kangri (Closed Reference)
treks.tagline: Famous 6,153 m trekking peak in Ladakh — currently CLOSED for ecological recovery
treks.statusNote: CLOSED SINCE 2020: Banned indefinitely by Ladakh Administration & ALLTOA to allow glacial and fragile trail recovery. Do NOT book illegal departures; choose Kang Yatse II (6,250 m) or Dzo Jongo instead.

permits.notes: No active climbing/trekking permits issued as of Nov 2026; listed transparently so planners are not misled by outdated itineraries.

treks.roadhead: Stok Village (3,500 m) — 15 km south of Leh
highlights: Historical flagship 6,000er south of the Indus Valley
Crucial conservation case study in halting over-tourism & glacier stress
Recommended ethical alternatives: Kang Yatse II / Markha / Yunam Peak

diyBudget.notes: Do not attempt unauthorized entry past Mankorma; book licensed Kang Yatse II or Markha circuits instead.

treks.summary: Once India's most celebrated 6,153 m climbable peak, Stok Kangri remains closed under joint Ladakh community and administration conservation decrees.

treks.name: Pin Parvati Pass
treks.tagline: Gruelling 110 km wilderness crossing linking Kullu's Parvati gorge to Spiti's Pin Valley
treks.region: Great Himalayan NP & Pin Valley NP
treks.statusNote: Requires IMF high-pass clearance & full glacial rope/crevasse team; solo trekking strongly discouraged due to crevassed snow bridges & whiteouts above Mantalai.

permits.authority: Kullu DDMA / GHNP / Pin Valley NP + IMF
permits.notes: Multi-jurisdiction forest/national park entry (~INR 300–500/day tiered tariff), high-pass Kullu DDMA (>15,000 ft) clearance; foreign citizens require Protected Area Permit for Spiti exit.

highlights: Immense 110 km self-contained glacial crossing above 5,300 m
Natural mud-rock stone bridge spanning the roaring Parvati River (Pandu Pul)
Sacred glacier lakehead at Mantalai (4,116 m)
Monsoon greenery fading to rust-purple Spiti canyons at Mudh

elevationProfile.camp: Pin Parvati Pass (5,319 m) to Wichkurung

diyBudget.notes: Requires experienced glacial guide + porters + technical rope/crampon/ice-axe hardware; DIY cost drops sharply with a 4–6 member experienced rope team.

treks.summary: A true Himalayan benchmark expedition bridging humid Kullu forests and stark Tibetan-plateau geology across an exposed glacier saddle above 5,300 m.

treks.name: Buran Ghati
treks.tagline: Pabbar alpine lakes culminating in a vertical snow-wall rappel down into Sangla orchards
treks.statusNote: Early-season May–Jun departures involve technical fixed-line rappel down the icy Kinnaur wall.

permits.notes: Standard ID entry at Janglik/Sangla exit; carries mandatory group rope & harness team for June cornice.

treks.roadhead: Janglik (2,800 m) via Rohru; exit at Barua (Kinnaur)
highlights: Wildflower-rich Dayara Thach meadow campsite (~3,375 m)
Twin waterfall cliff cirque leading to Chandranahan Lake (4,023 m)
Thrilling fixed-rope descent off Buran Pass cornice in early summer
Apple orchard villages cascading toward Baspa River at Barua

diyBudget.notes: HRTC buses connect Shimla ISBT to Chirgaon/Rohru cheaply; always include technical harness + rope hire for pass day.

treks.summary: A visual kaleidoscope cramming dense oak woods, cascading lake walls, glacier passes, and vertical snow-wall rappelling cleanly inside a single week.

treks.name: Kashmir Great Lakes
treks.tagline: Three 4,000 m passes threading past Vishansar, Kishansar, Gadsar, Satsar & Gangabal lakes
treks.statusNote: Check security advisories before Sonamarg check-in; **only postpaid SIM cards work in J&K** (no mobile coverage once past Shitkadi).

permits.authority: J&K Wildlife Protection / Police & Army Registration (Sonamarg)
permits.notes: Original govt photo ID + photocopies mandatory at Shitkadi & Gadsar army checkposts; subject to active security clearance.

treks.roadhead: Shitkadi, Sonamarg (2,600 m); exit Naranag (2,250 m)
highlights: Turquoise glacial basins mirroring Harmukh Peak (5,142 m)
Three 4,000 m+ pass traverses: Nichnai, Gadsar, and Zaj Pass
Seven interconnected high tarns across Satsar plateau
Wildflower shepherd grazing downs beneath dramatic cirque spires

diyBudget.notes: Requires full self-contained camping + ration/pony hire between Shitkadi and Naranag; Sonamarg Tourist Reception Centre lists local pony/guide tariffs.

treks.summary: Unrivaled concentration of jewel-toned glacial tarns across rolling Kashmir meadows when monsoon saturates most of Uttarakhand and Himachal.

treks.name: Kuari Pass (Lord Curzon Trail)
treks.tagline: Balcony ridge opening direct sightlines onto Nanda Devi, Kamet, and Dronagiri
treks.statusNote: Medical fitness checkup fee (~INR 300) may be checked locally in Joshimath; landslide advisories apply along NH-7 during heavy monsoon.

permits.authority: Nanda Devi National Park / Joshimath Forest Office
permits.notes: Forest entry + medical check certification required at Joshimath forest office before proceeding to Tugasi.

highlights: Grand amphitheater facing Nanda Devi (7,816 m), Dronagiri, Kamet & Chaukhamba
Golden oak and silver birch canopy over Gulling Top
High winter ridge crossing between Khullara and Tali Lake
Optional side traverse across Auli's undulating Gorson Bugyal

diyBudget.notes: Shared Tata Sumo from Haridwar/Rishikesh bus stand to Joshimath (~INR 600–700 each way) plus shared local jeep up to Tugasi trailhead.

treks.summary: Explored famously as Lord Curzon's trail in 1905, Kuari Pass rewards first-time winter trekkers with some of the highest uninterrupted 7,000 m+ mountain horizons in India.
